item.text:
I continued by centralizing grid traversal in [Field.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/R006_module_java/Field.java:14). It now exposes reusable traversal hooks like `forEachLocation`, `forEachOccupiedLocation`, `forEachStoredActor`, and `forEachAnimalBlock`, so callers no longer duplicate nested row/column loops or block-scanning logic.

That let [SimulatorView.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/R006_module_java/SimulatorView.java:191), [FieldStats.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/R006_module_java/FieldStats.java:111), [PopulationGenerator.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/R006_module_java/PopulationGenerator.java:71), and [DiseaseHandler.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/R006_module_java/DiseaseHandler.java:45) collapse their custom traversal code and depend on `Field` as the single place that defines how the grid is walked. The split between `forEachOccupiedLocation` and `forEachStoredActor` also makes the animal-over-plant rendering rule explicit instead of implicit in multiple callers.

Verification: the refactored core simulation classes compile successfully with temporary UI stubs. Full project compilation is still blocked here by the existing JavaFX dependency in `Dashboard.java`.
